transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey. Um... I guess I'm here about my diet. I'm a firefighter, and I've been aiming for the lieutenant track, so I started trying to eat cleaner a while back. But... I don't know. It kind of turned into me just cutting my meals down a lot. 

Like, lately I'm mostly just having black coffee, maybe a protein shake, and a really small dinner. Even on shift days, when I know for a fact I'm burning way more than that. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Are you trying to lose weight or avoid gaining weight with your current eating habits?

I guess... mostly just avoid gaining it. 

Um. It's just... if the scale is up even a pound, like after a big meal at the station or just extra water, I kind of... I don't know. I get this tight feeling. Like a panic, almost. Like I've blown it and... people are going to see me as soft. Or out of control. 

So... yeah. I just try to keep it down.
Do you think about your weight or body shape every day?

Yeah... I guess I do. 

Like... before work, I check the mirror. Mostly just looking at my waist, or... if my face looks sharp enough. If it doesn't... I don't know. It just kind of throws me off. Makes me feel less... confident, I guess. Less ready to take charge on shift.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform specific rituals or behaviors to cope with your anxiety about weight or body shape?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, I just... I check the mirror like I said, but... I don't really have any rituals or anything like that. Just... trying to stick to the plan.
Do you feel an overwhelming urge to engage in excessive exercise to burn off calories or maintain your weight?

No... not overwhelming, no. I just... I work out because of my job. You have to be fit to be a firefighter. So I run, do some lifting... but it's just part of the job. I don't... I don't have to do it to burn calories or anything. Just staying in shape.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I mean... I guess I've dropped some. 

My turnout gear feels a lot looser lately. Same with my station uniform. It just... hangs off me a bit more. We had a fitness review recently and they... they actually flagged me. Said I was too light for my height and build. 

But... I don't know. Even with them saying that, I still feel like... maybe I could just trim down a little bit more. Just to be safe.
Do you think you would still try to restrict your food intake even if you weren't worried about being seen as soft by others?
I don't know. I guess... I mean, the food thing is just... it's just what I do now. I don't really think about it like that. I just want to keep things under control.
Do you think you would still want to eat as little as you do now if you didn't care about what others think of your appearance?
I'm not sure. I haven't really thought about it like that. I just... I just eat what I eat.
Do you think you would still want to restrict your food intake if you could maintain your current weight without changing your eating habits?

I don't know... maybe. It's just... I came in because, well, I started out just trying to eat cleaner. You know, for the lieutenant track. But... now it's just... I'm basically down to black coffee and a protein shake during the day, and then a small dinner. Even on shift days, when I know I'm burning a lot more than that. It's just kind of... what I do now.
Would you say that your main goal with your current eating habits is to avoid gaining weight?

I guess... yeah. It's just, if I check the scale and it's up even a pound... like after a big station meal or just extra water... I get this... I don't know, this tight panic. Like I completely blew it. I just don't want people thinking I'm soft, or... out of control.
Do you have a specific weight or body shape in mind that you're trying to achieve with your current eating habits?

Not really an exact number, I guess. It's more just... I don't know. When I look in the mirror before work, I mostly just check if my waist and face look sharp enough. And if they don't... it just kind of messes with me. Like it changes how confident I feel, or... whether I feel command-ready for the shift. So I just try to keep it sharp.
Do you feel like your concerns about weight and body shape are unreasonable or excessive?
I don't know. I guess... not really? It just feels like what I need to do right now. I haven't really thought of it as excessive... it's just how I keep on track.
Do you feel like you would still be checking your weight or body shape as frequently if you didn't have to present yourself in a certain way for your job as a firefighter?
I'm not sure. I mean... maybe? I've never really thought about it like that. It's just... it's just what I do.
Do you think your concerns about your weight and body shape would decrease if you were no longer a firefighter?
I don't really know. Hard to say. I mean... I'm not planning on leaving the department, so... I haven't really pictured it. It's just kind of my routine right now, I guess.
Do you think you would still be as concerned about your weight and body shape if you were in a different profession?
I mean... like I said, I don't really know. I've only ever done this job, so... it's hard to picture. Probably? I just... I don't really think about doing anything else.
Do you think you would still be worried about your weight if you didn't care about how your body looks?
I... I don't really get what you mean. I guess if I didn't care, then... maybe not? But... I don't know. It's just kind of a weird hypothetical. I haven't really thought about it.
Do you think your concerns about your weight and body shape are more because of how you want to see yourself or because of how you think others see you as a firefighter?

I guess... it's mostly about how I see myself. Like, when I look in the mirror before work... I just sort of focus on whether my waist and my face look sharp enough. And... I don't know, if they don't, it just kind of messes with my confidence for the shift. I just don't feel as... command-ready, I guess. So, yeah. Mostly me.
Do you think you would still want to eat as little as you do now if you could maintain your current weight without restricting your food intake?

I... I don't know. Maybe. I mean, it started out just trying to eat cleaner, you know? Because I'm trying to get on the lieutenant track. But... I guess it kind of shifted. Now I'm just... I'll have black coffee, maybe a protein shake, and just a small dinner. Even on shift days when we're running hard and I know I burned off way more than that. So... I'm not sure if it's just about the weight anymore.
Do you think you would still be as strict with your eating habits if nobody, including your colleagues and superiors at the fire department, knew about your weight or body shape?
I... I guess so. I mean, it's not really about them. Like I said, it's more about... how I feel about myself. So, yeah, I think I'd probably still do the same thing. It's just... what I do now.
